mainTopic: Redeeming an עבד עברי leniently, and the rules for redeeming a sold field versus a field given to הקדש
overview: אביי says he is ready for any question, and a Sage asks why we read the פסוקים about redeeming an עבד עברי in the slave's favor. אביי answers that the תורה is clearly kind to an עבד עברי, since the master must give him food, drink and bedding equal to his own. The Sage argues for strictness using רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's chain: dealing in שביעית produce leads a person, step by step, to sell his possessions, his field, his house, his daughter, and finally himself, even to serve עבודה זרה. Along the way, רב הונא explains that a sin done twice comes to feel permitted. אביי answers that the תורה still insists the man be redeemed. רב נחמן בר יצחק then proves from the extra word ״בשנים״ that he is always redeemed at the lower price, and רב יוסף praises this as true as if from סיני. The גמרא next finds sources for the משנה's rule that a sold field may not be redeemed with a loan, with money from selling another field, or in parts. רבא explains why ״ומצא״ means different things in different פסוקים. Finally, a ברייתא and רבי שמעון explain why a field redeemed from הקדש may be redeemed in all these easier ways.

steps.title: אביי announces he is ready for any question
steps.stepSummary: אביי declares that he is ready to answer questions like בן עזאי used to do in the markets of טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: I am like בן עזאי in the markets of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי invites challenges by comparing himself to בן עזאי, who was famous for answering any question in public. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a ruling. It is an opening line that invites a challenge. The next step is a Sage taking אביי up on his offer.

keyTerms.meaning: Here I am / I am hereby
The markets of טבריא, where בן עזאי would teach and answer questions

phrases.english: I am like Ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias.
phrases.notes: These are אביי's words. He means: ask me anything, I'm ready, just like בן עזאי was.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי כְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּשׁוּקֵי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of this section; invites the question that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. אביי declares his readiness to answer challenges.

steps.title: Why read the slave's redemption verses leniently?
steps.stepSummary: A Sage challenges אביי: the פסוקים about redeeming an עבד עברי could be read to help him or to be strict with him, so why choose leniency?
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to אביי: These פסוקים could be explained in the slave's favor, and they could be explained against him. Why do you say in his favor? Say against him!
steps.whatsHappening: A Sage takes up אביי's offer and challenges the way we read the redemption פסוקים of an עבד עברי. He asks why we always choose the reading that helps the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sage points out that the פסוקים could fairly be read in either direction. If both readings are possible, there needs to be a reason to prefer the lenient one. He pushes אביי to justify that choice.

keyTerms.meaning: To expound them (the פסוקים)
In a lenient way (in the slave's favor)
In a strict way (against the slave)
From where do we know? / What makes you say?

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Abaye:
It is possible to expound them as a leniency,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the פסוקים about redeeming a Hebrew slave, which the גמרא was discussing just before this.

phrases.english: and it is possible to expound them as a stringency.
From where do we know that it is as a leniency?
Say it is as a stringency!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דִּלְקוּלָּא? אֵימָא לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up אביי's invitation with a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted lenient reading of the פסוקים about redeeming an עבד עברי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוקים can be read either way, there is no clear reason to pick the lenient reading over the strict one.

steps.title: The Torah is clearly lenient with a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תורה itself goes easy on an עבד עברי. A ברייתא says the master must give him food, drink and bedding equal to his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. The תורה was lenient with him, as a ברייתא teaches: "Because he fares well with you." With you in food and with you in drink. You may not eat fine bread while he eats coarse bread, drink old wine while he drinks new wine, or sleep on soft cushions while he sleeps on the ground. From here they said: Someone who buys an עבד עברי is like someone who buys a master for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. Since the תורה clearly shows kindness to an עבד עברי, we should also read the redemption פסוקים in his favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue from the redemption פסוקים themselves. He brings a general pattern: the תורה requires the master to treat the slave as his equal. This tells us the תורה's overall attitude toward the slave is lenient, which decides the unclear case.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind (don't think that)
The Merciful One (the תורה)
Coarse bread made from rough flour mixed with bran
Soft material such as cushions or soft bedding
A Hebrew (Jewish) slave
Like buying a master for himself

steps.whatToRemember: The famous line "הקונה עבד עברי כקונה אדון לעצמו" comes from here. The master must give his עבד עברי living conditions equal to his own.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
since the Merciful One was lenient with him,
as it is taught: "Because he fares well with you"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:16

phrases.english: with you in food, with you in drink,
that you should not be eating fine bread
while he eats coarse bread,
you drinking old wine
while he drinks new wine,
phrases.notes: Old wine was the better quality; new wine was considered inferior.

phrases.english: you sleeping on soft cushions
while he sleeps on the ground.
From here they said:

phrases.aramaic: הַקּוֹנֶה עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כְּקוֹנֶה אָדוֹן לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: One who acquires a Hebrew slave is like one who acquires a master for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּיךְ, מִדְּאַקֵּיל רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the Sage's challenge from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the תורה's overall lenient attitude toward the עבד עברי, shown in a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The redemption פסוקים might be read strictly against the slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the תורה requires the master to treat the slave as an equal, unclear פסוקים about him are read leniently.

steps.title: On the contrary: be strict, based on רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The Sage pushes back and says we should be strict with the slave. He brings רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching about how severe even a small breach of שביעית is.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, let us be strict with him, because of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: "Come and see how severe even the 'dust' of שביעית is."
steps.whatsHappening: The Sage turns אביי's answer around and argues for strictness. He starts quoting רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, and the details of that teaching come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sage is pointing to a teaching that shows how a person ends up poor and sold, step by step, because of a sin connected to שביעית. If being sold as a slave is the result of sin, perhaps the תורה wants us to be strict with him, not lenient. This step only opens the quote; the next step gives its content.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Let us be strict
Come and see
Its 'dust': a small, minor side-issue of a prohibition
The Sabbatical (seventh) year

steps.confusionAlert: "אבק" here does not mean real dust. It means a minor, secondary part of the prohibition. Here that is doing business with שביעית produce rather than the main prohibition of working the land.

phrases.english: On the contrary, let us be strict with him
because of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina!
For Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
"Come and see how severe
is the 'dust' of the Sabbatical Year."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, נַחְמִיר עֲלֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 3 by arguing for the opposite conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the תורה's attitude toward the עבד עברי is lenient.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching suggests a person is sold because of sin, which could argue for strictness toward him.

steps.title: Trading in Sabbatical produce leads to selling one's possessions
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching continues. Someone who does business with שביעית produce ends up selling his movable possessions, as shown by the order of the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person does business with שביעית produce, and in the end he sells his movable possessions. As it says: "In this יובל year each man shall return to his possession," and right after it is written: "And if you sell something to your fellow or buy from the hand of your fellow." This means something acquired from hand to hand.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the content of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching, which the Sage is using to argue for strictness. Placing the פסוק about selling right after the פסוק about יובל shows that breaking those laws leads to selling one's possessions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from two פסוקים placed one after the other. The second one speaks of buying "from the hand," which means מטלטלין, things passed from hand to hand. The lesson is that the sin brings poverty, starting with having to sell movable property.

keyTerms.meaning: Does business / trades
Produce of the Sabbatical year, which may not be traded for profit
His movable possessions
The Jubilee (fiftieth) year
From hand to hand: describes movable items

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first stage of a longer chain in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching. The Sage uses that chain to suggest that someone who reaches slavery got there through sin.

phrases.english: A person does business with produce of the Sabbatical Year;
in the end he sells his movable property,
as it is said: "In this Jubilee Year
you shall return every man to his possession,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:13

phrases.english: and it is written: "And if you sell something to your neighbor
or buy from your neighbor's hand,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:14, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: an item that is acquired from hand to hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם נוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית, לְסוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת מִטַּלְטְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaching introduced in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The Sage's claim that we should be strict with the עבד עברי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of ויקרא 25:13-14, as read by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: If he still does not feel it, he ends up selling his fields
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא continues: if the person does not feel remorse, he will end up selling his fields, as the next פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not feel it, in the end he sells his fields, as it says: 'If your brother becomes poor and sells from his ancestral land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the chain from step 5. If the person still does not wake up and do תשובה, the next stage is that he has to sell his fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof again comes from the order of the פסוקים. Right after the section about movable things comes 'וּמָכַר מֵאֲחֻזָּתוֹ', which is about selling ancestral land. So the punishment gets heavier: first movable things, now land.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, eventually
He did not feel it, he did not sense that he was being punished and needed to do תשובה
Ancestral land, a family's inherited field

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת שְׂדוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: If he did not feel it, in the end he sells his fields,
phrases.notes: He means: he didn't notice that losing his movable things was a message to do תשובה.

phrases.english: as it says: "If your brother becomes poor
and sells from his ancestral land."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:25

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת שְׂדוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's chain from step 5 with the next stage of loss.
steps.raayaObject: That someone who deals in שביעית produce and does not do תשובה will end up selling his fields.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the פסוקים in ויקרא 25: the land-selling פסוק (25:25) comes after the section on selling movable things.

steps.title: If it does not come to his attention, he ends up selling his house
steps.stepSummary: The next stage: if he still does not realize, he will sell his house, as the following פסוק talks about selling a house in a walled city.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it did not come to his attention, in the end he sells his house, as it says: 'And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The chain goes one step further. If he still does not do תשובה, he loses even the house he lives in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the proof is the order of the פסוקים: after selling land comes selling a house in an עיר חומה. Notice the wording changes here from 'לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ' to 'לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ'. The גמרא will ask about this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'it did not come to his hand': it did not even reach his awareness
A dwelling house, the home a person lives in
A walled city

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: If it did not come to his attention, in the end he sells his house,
phrases.notes: Literally 'it did not come to his hand.' He means the idea of doing תשובה never even reached him.

phrases.english: as it says: "And if a man sells
a dwelling house in a walled city."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:29

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next link in the same chain, with slightly different wording.
steps.raayaObject: That if he still does not do תשובה, he will end up selling his house.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:29, which comes after the land-selling פסוק.

steps.title: Why does the wording change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first stage says 'he did not feel it' while the next stage says 'it did not come to his attention.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, where it says 'he did not feel,' and what is different here, where it says 'it did not come to his attention'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the chain to ask about the words. It wants to know why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא changed his wording between the two stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that a change in wording means something. 'לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ' sounds like he missed the feeling of regret. 'לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ' sounds like it never even entered his mind. The question is what caused this shift.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asking why two cases are treated differently
There, the earlier case
Here, the current case

phrases.english: What is different there, where he says "he did not feel,"
phrases.notes: 'There' means the fields stage in step 6.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּקָאָמַר ״לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ״?
phrases.english: and what is different here, where he says "it did not come to his attention"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pauses the chain to ask about the change in wording between steps 6 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the wording changes from 'לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ' to 'לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ'.

steps.title: רב הונא: a repeated sin becomes permitted to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב הונא's teaching: once a person does a sin and repeats it, it becomes 'permitted' to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב הונא, for רב הונא said: once a person does a sin and repeats it, it is permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording question by bringing רב הונא. By the later stage the person has sinned again and again, so the sin no longer even registers with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the first stage, he still could have felt regret, so the text says 'he did not feel.' After repeating the sin, it feels normal to him, so now it does not even 'come to his attention.' The odd words 'הוּתְּרָה לוֹ' will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the teaching of (a certain רב)
A sin
He repeated it, did it a second time
It became permitted to him

steps.whyThisMatters: רב הונא's idea is a well-known lesson in מוסר: doing a sin twice dulls a person's sense that it is wrong.

phrases.english: It is like רב הונא,
for רב הונא said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר אָדָם עֲבֵירָה וְשָׁנָה בָּהּ,
phrases.english: once a person commits a sin and repeats it,
it is permitted to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By the later stage he has repeated the sin, so it no longer registers as a sin. That is why the wording becomes 'it did not come to his attention.'

steps.title: Can a sin really become permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב הונא's wording: how can you think a sin actually becomes permitted just because he did it twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is permitted to him' — could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the words 'הוּתְּרָה לוֹ'. Doing a sin twice cannot really make it allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, רב הונא's words would mean that repeating a sin makes it allowed, which is impossible. So the גמרא shows that this reading cannot be right. This sets up the corrected wording in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? A way of saying 'that can't be right'

phrases.english: "It is permitted to him" — could that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּתְּרָה לוֹ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal wording of רב הונא's statement from step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin cannot become truly permitted just because someone repeated it, so the literal reading is impossible.

steps.title: It becomes like something permitted to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the sin does not become permitted, it just feels to him as if it were permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: it becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב הונא's words. The sin is still forbidden, but in his own eyes it now feels allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is in the wording: not 'הוּתְּרָה לוֹ', it is permitted to him, but 'נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר', it becomes to him like something permitted. This is about how the person feels, not about the הלכה. That fits the earlier wording: after repeating the sin, the idea of תשובה does not even reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: a way of correcting the wording
Like something permitted

steps.whatToRemember: A sin done twice does not become allowed, but it starts to feel allowed. That is why the later stages say 'it did not come to his attention.'
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רב הונא as a הלכה that the sin is allowed. It is only describing how it feels to the sinner.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it becomes to him like something permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 10 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא seemed to say the repeated sin actually becomes permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only feels permitted to the sinner, so he no longer even notices it.

steps.title: If he still does not realize, he ends up borrowing with interest
steps.stepSummary: Back to the chain: if it still does not come to his attention, he will end up borrowing with ריבית, as the פסוקים about a poor brother and interest show.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it did not come to his attention, in the end he borrows with interest, as it says: 'And if your brother becomes poor...' and it is written: 'Do not take from him interest or increase.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's chain. The next stage is that he becomes so poor that he must borrow money and pay ריבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the proof is from the order of the פסוקים. The פסוק 'וְכִי יָמוּךְ אָחִיךָ' about a brother who became poor is followed by the ban on taking נשך ותרבית from him. So the poor man in the story is now someone who borrows with interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrows
Interest on a loan
And so on: the פסוק continues
Two names in the תורה for forbidden interest

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁלֹּוֶה בְּרִבִּית,
phrases.english: If it did not come to his attention, in the end he borrows with interest,
as it says: "And if your brother becomes poor, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:35

phrases.english: and it is written: "Do not take from him
interest or increase."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36, the very next פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁלֹּוֶה בְּרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about wording, returns to the chain of downfall.
steps.raayaObject: That if he still does not do תשובה, he will end up borrowing with ריבית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:35-36: the poor brother פסוק followed by the ban on taking interest from him.

steps.title: Before he borrows with interest, he has already sold his daughter
steps.stepSummary: If he still does not notice, he does not reach borrowing with ריבית until he has already sold his daughter, as the פסוק about a man selling his daughter shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it still does not come to his attention, [he does not reach borrowing with interest] until he has sold his daughter, as the פסוק says: 'And when a man sells his daughter as a maidservant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a stage to the ladder: by the time he borrows with ריבית, he has already sold his daughter. It brings a פסוק for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the other stages, this פסוק is not from ויקרא 25. It comes from שמות, about selling a daughter as an אמה. The next step explains why it still belongs in the chain, and why it comes before ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: It did not come to his attention (he still did not wake up)
A Jewish maidservant (a young girl sold by her father)
Sells his daughter

phrases.english: If it did not come to his attention —
[he does not come to it] until he has sold his daughter,
as it is said:
'And when a man sells his daughter as a maidservant,'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — עַד שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain one stage past borrowing with ריבית.
steps.raayaObject: That the next stage of decline is selling his daughter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 21:7: 'וכי ימכור איש את בתו לאמה'.

steps.title: Why selling a daughter comes after borrowing with interest
steps.stepSummary: The daughter is not mentioned in this section, but a person would rather sell his daughter than borrow with ריבית, because her redemption price goes down while interest keeps going up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though his daughter is not mentioned in this section, a person prefers to sell his daughter rather than borrow with interest. There, her price keeps going down. Here, the debt keeps going up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: why is selling a daughter placed in this chain, and why after ריבית? It explains that people choose selling a daughter before taking an interest loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hidden difficulty has two parts. The daughter is not in the פרשה in ויקרא, and selling a child sounds worse than borrowing. The answer is practical: a sold daughter's redemption amount shrinks over time, while an interest debt grows. So anyone who reached ריבית has already sold his daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: She is not mentioned in this section
A person prefers
It keeps decreasing
It keeps increasing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the order as 'first ריבית, then the daughter.' The גמרא is saying the opposite: a person facing ריבית has already sold his daughter, because he would choose that first.

phrases.english: And even though his daughter
is not in this section,
phrases.notes: He means the section in ויקרא 25 about a poor brother, where the other stages come from.

phrases.english: a person prefers to sell his daughter
and not borrow with interest,
because there it keeps going down,
phrases.notes: The amount needed to redeem the daughter gets smaller as her years of service pass.

phrases.english: while here it keeps going up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּבִתּוֹ בְּהַאי עִנְיָנָא לֵיתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the daughter stage belongs in the chain, even though it comes from a different פרשה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing 'selling his daughter' in a chain built on ויקרא 25, where she is not mentioned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unspoken: the daughter is not in this section, and the order seems odd.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical human reasoning about which choice people make first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling a daughter seems unrelated to this chain, or worse than borrowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: People sell a daughter before borrowing with ריבית, since her redemption price shrinks while interest grows.

steps.title: Next stage: he sells himself, even to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: Still not waking up, he sells himself. First he is sold to a Jew, then to a גר, then even to a גר תושב, each stage learned from the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it still does not come to his attention, in the end he sells himself, as it says: 'If your brother becomes poor with you and is sold to you.' Not only to you, but even to a stranger, as it says 'to the stranger.' And not only to a convert, but even to a גר תושב, as it says 'to a גר תושב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues down the ladder: now he sells himself as a slave. It shows from the פסוקים that he sinks lower and lower in who buys him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוקים is read as a further drop. First 'to you,' a fellow Jew. Then 'to a גר,' a convert. Then 'to a גר תושב,' a non-Jew who only keeps the seven Noahide laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Sells himself as a slave
A full convert to Judaism
A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who accepted the seven Noahide laws

phrases.english: If it did not come to his attention —
in the end he sells himself,
as it is said: 'If your brother becomes poor with you
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:39.

phrases.english: and is sold to you';
not only to you, but even to a stranger,
as it is said: 'to the stranger,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:47.

phrases.english: and not only to a convert,
but even to a resident non-Jew,
as it is said: 'to a resident stranger.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ — לַסּוֹף שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next stage after selling his daughter.
steps.raayaObject: That he sinks to selling himself, even to a גר תושב.

steps.title: The lowest point: serving idol worship itself
steps.stepSummary: 'A stranger's family' means an idol-worshipping non-Jew. 'The offshoot of a stranger's family' means he is sold to work for the idol worship itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A stranger's family': this is the non-Jew. When it says 'or to the offshoot of a stranger's family,' this is one who is sold and becomes a servant to the idol worship itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the chain by reading the last words of the פסוק as the very bottom. He is sold to serve in an idol's temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'משפחת גר' goes one step below the גר תושב, to a regular idol-worshipping non-Jew. The word 'עקר' is read as the idol itself, so he ends up as a worker for עבודה זרה. That ends the ladder of decline that began with dealing in שביעית produce.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'offshoot' of a stranger's family, read here as idol worship itself
A servant working for idol worship
A non-Jew (here, an idol worshipper)

steps.whatToRemember: The full chain: sells שביעית produce → sells his movable things → his field → his house → borrows with ריבית (having already sold his daughter) → sells himself to a Jew → to a גר → to a גר תושב → to an idol-worshipping non-Jew → to serve עבודה זרה itself.

phrases.english: 'A stranger's family' — this is the non-Jew.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:47.

phrases.english: When it says
'or to the offshoot of a stranger's family' —
this is one who is sold and becomes a servant
to the idol worship itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁפַּחַת גֵּר — זֶה הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the chain with its last and lowest stages.
steps.raayaObject: That he ends up sold to an idolater, and even to serve idol worship itself.

steps.title: But the פסוק insists he be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests he fell this low because of his sins, so maybe we should be strict with him. The response is that the פסוק brings him back, as דבי רבי ישמעאל taught: he has a right of redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But the פסוק brings him back! As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Since he went and sold himself to idol worship, should we push another stone after the one who fell? The פסוק says: 'He shall have redemption forever, and in the יובל he goes free.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the Sage's challenge from step 4. The Sage argued that since sin brought the man to slavery, we should be strict with him. אביי replies with a ברייתא showing that the תורה still insists he be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could suggest that this man brought his fate on himself, so we owe him nothing special. The response, which the standard explanation attributes to אביי, says the פסוק 'returns him': it gives him a right of redemption and freedom in the יובל. So we do not abandon a fallen person.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק brought him back (requires him to be redeemed)
Should I throw a stone after the one who fell? (kick him when he's down)
Redemption, buying him back out of slavery
The fiftieth year, when slaves go free

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic Torah attitude. Even a Jew who sank to the very lowest point through his own sins is not written off. The תורה commands that he be redeemed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
But the verse brings him back!
And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Since he went and sold himself
to idol worship,
should I push a stone after the one who fell?
The verse teaches:
'He shall have redemption forever,
phrases.notes: This mixes phrases from ויקרא 25 (see 25:31, 48). 25:48 is the one about a Jew sold to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: and in the Jubilee he goes free.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אַהְדְּרֵיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי's reply to the Sage's challenge of step 4, which was built on the chain in steps 5-16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that, since sin brought him there, we should be strict about redeeming him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה explicitly requires his redemption and frees him in the יובל, even after he sold himself to idol worship. So his sin is not a reason to abandon him.

steps.title: Redemption yes, but a strict price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the פסוק only means he must be redeemed so he is not lost among the non-Jews. When it comes to calculating his redemption, we can still be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'He shall have redemption' means so that he will not be swallowed up among the non-Jews. But when it comes to the details of redeeming him, we will be strict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 17. It agrees he must be redeemed, but says this does not mean the redemption has to be done in a lenient way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof showed the תורה wants him redeemed. The push-back narrows that: the reason is only to stop him from assimilating among the non-Jews. That goal is met even with a strict redemption calculation, so his sin can still justify strictness about the price.

keyTerms.meaning: To be swallowed up and assimilated among the non-Jews
Redemption, the act or price of buying him free
We will be strict

steps.confusionAlert: The push-back does not say we leave him enslaved. It agrees he must be redeemed. It only argues about how strictly we calculate his redemption.

phrases.english: Say: 'He shall have redemption' —
so that he will not be assimilated among the non-Jews,
but really, regarding his redemption, we will be strict!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: גְּאוּלָּה תִּהְיֶה לוֹ — דְּלָא לִיטַּמַּע בַּגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 17 by limiting what the פסוק requires.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial. It accepts that he must be redeemed but rejects the conclusion that the redemption must be handled leniently.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's goal (not being lost among the non-Jews) is met even with strict terms, so it does not show leniency about the redemption itself.

steps.title: Two verses show the redemption price is always the lower amount
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the פסוקים speak of 'many in the years' and 'few in the years.' Years cannot be long or short, so he explains them as talking about the slave's money value going up or down. In each case the slave pays the cheaper amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: One פסוק says 'If there are yet many in the years,' and the next says 'If there remain but few in the years.' Are there years that are long and years that are short? Rather, if his value went up, he pays 'from the money he was bought for.' If his value went down, he pays 'according to his years.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a proof from the פסוקים that we are lenient, not strict, when figuring out how much the slave pays to be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A year is always a year, so 'many' and 'few' cannot describe the years themselves. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads them as describing the slave's value. If his value rose, he pays based on the old, lower purchase price. If his value dropped, he pays based on his current, lower value. Either way he pays less, which goes against the strict approach suggested in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: The money he was bought for, the original purchase price
According to his years, meaning his value now
His money value went up
His money value went down
Redemption, buying the slave back to freedom

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'many' and 'few' as the number of years left. That is exactly the reading the גמרא rejects in the next steps. Here they describe whether his money value went up or down.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for redeeming a Jew sold to a non-Jew: he always gets the lower price, so we are lenient with him.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is written: "If there are yet many in the years,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:51

phrases.english: And it is written: "If there remain but few in the years."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:52, the very next פסוק.

phrases.english: But are there years that are many (long)
and years that are few (short)?
phrases.notes: He means every year is the same length, so these words must be teaching something else.

phrases.english: Rather: if his money value went up,
he pays "from the money he was bought for";
phrases.notes: That is the older, lower price.

phrases.english: if his money value went down,
he pays "according to his years."
phrases.notes: That means his value now, which is lower.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the strict approach of Step 18 by showing from the פסוקים that the calculation is lenient.
steps.raayaObject: That the redemption price is calculated leniently, always using the lower amount.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:51-52: the strange phrases 'many in the years' and 'few in the years.'

steps.title: Maybe the verses mean how many years are left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading: 'many' and 'few' refer to how many years of work are still left. Then the slave would simply pay for the remaining years, with no leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: when he worked two years and four are left, he pays for four, as 'from the money he was bought for.' When he worked four years and two are left, he pays for two, as 'according to his years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק by offering a simpler reading of the פסוקים that has nothing to do with the value going up or down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'many years' means many years are still left and 'few years' means few are left. The slave just pays for whatever time remains. If this is right, the פסוקים do not prove that we are lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: But say, introducing a different possible reading
That he worked (served)
They remain, are left over
Two

phrases.english: But say: where he worked two years
and four years remain,
let him pay him for four years, "from the money he was bought for";
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is the owner who bought him.

phrases.english: and where he worked four years
and two years remain,
let him pay him for two years, "according to his years"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: הֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּי וּפָיְישִׁי אַרְבְּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how Step 19 read the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading that 'many' and 'few' refer to the slave's value going up or down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrases can be read more simply as the number of years left to serve, so they give no proof of leniency.

steps.title: The extra word 'in the years' proves the value reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the פסוק only meant the number of years left, it would say 'many years.' The extra word 'בַּשָּׁנִים' (in the years) shows it means the value went up or down during the years of service.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have written 'If there are yet many years.' Why does it say 'in the years'? To teach: if his value went up during the years, he pays 'from the money he was bought for.' If his value went down during the years, he pays 'according to his years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן בר יצחק by pointing to an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To say 'many years are left,' the תורה only needed 'רַבּוֹת שָׁנִים.' Adding 'בַּשָּׁנִים' means something changed 'in the years,' namely his value. So the reading from Step 19 stands, and the slave always pays the lower amount.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, used to show that a suggestion leads to a problem
Let it write, meaning the פסוק should have said
In the years, the extra word the דרשה depends on

steps.whatToRemember: The extra 'ב' in 'בַּשָּׁנִים' shows the פסוקים are about the slave's value changing over the years, so he is always redeemed at the lower price.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב ״אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת שָׁנִים״,
phrases.english: If so, let it write: "If there are yet many years";
what is "in the years"?
phrases.notes: The extra letter ב, 'in,' is what the גמרא is learning from.

phrases.english: If his money value went up during the years,
he pays "from the money he was bought for";
if his money value went down during the years,
he pays "according to his years."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב ״אִם עוֹד רַבּוֹת שָׁנִים״, מַאי ״בַּשָּׁנִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the other reading in Step 20 and confirms Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק rules out the other reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים might just mean the number of years left to serve.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'בַּשָּׁנִים' shows they refer to his value changing over the years, so he always pays the lower amount.

steps.title: רב יוסף praises the derasha as true as from סיני
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that רב נחמן explained these פסוקים as accurately as if the explanation had been given at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב נחמן explained these פסוקים as if they were from סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The section ends with רב יוסף's strong praise for רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This praise seals the conclusion. The lenient way of calculating the redemption, always the lower amount, is accepted as the true meaning of the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained them (interpreted the פסוקים)
Verses
Like at סיני, as true as if given to משה

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: a Jew sold to a non-Jew is redeemed at the lower amount, the purchase price if his value went up and his current value if it went down. רב יוסף praised this reading as being like from סיני.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: דַּרְשִׁינְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Rav Nachman explained
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן בר יצחק from the start of this section.

phrases.english: these verses as if from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: דַּרְשִׁינְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי כְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seals the reading defended in Step 21 with praise.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading is accepted: the redemption is always calculated at the lower, more lenient amount.

steps.title: Where does the rule against selling a far field to redeem come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about not selling a distant field to redeem, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he may not sell a far field (to redeem a near one), etc. From where do we know these rules?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה and asking for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of the משנה are not written plainly in the תורה, so the גמרא wants to know which words of the פסוק teach them. The word ״כו׳" tells us the whole משנה line is meant, including the rules about borrowing and redeeming in halves.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned? (asking for a source)
far; here, a field in a distant place
etc., meaning the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: He may not sell a distant [field], etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: he may not sell a far field to buy back his ancestral field that is nearby.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after רב יוסף's praise of רב נחמן in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the משנה's limits on how a seller may redeem his field.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns three rules from the words of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ״והשיגה ידו״, ״ומצא״ and ״כדי גאולתו״ as three separate limits on redeeming the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "And his hand attains" means his own hand, so he may not borrow money and redeem. "And finds" leaves out money he already had, so he may not sell a far field and redeem a near one, or sell a poor field and redeem a good one. "Enough for its redemption" means he redeems only when he has enough for the whole field. He does not redeem it in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that takes each phrase of ויקרא 25:26 and learns one rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״והשיגה ידו״ means the money must be his own, so no loans. ״ומצא״ means newly found money, so he may not sell property he already owned. ״כדי גאולתו״ means the full amount, so no paying in parts.

keyTerms.meaning: "and his hand attains", meaning he himself has the money
excluding what was already available to him
redemption; buying back the sold field
in halves; partly now and partly later

steps.whatToRemember: Three limits: no borrowed money (״ידו״), no money from selling property he already owned (״ומצא״), and no redeeming in parts (״כדי גאולתו״).

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"And his hand attains"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:26

phrases.english: his own hand,
that he may not borrow and redeem.
"And finds": excluding what was already available,
that he may not sell a distant [field] and redeem a near one,
[or sell] a poor one and redeem a good one;
"enough for its redemption"
with enough for the [whole] redemption he redeems,
and he does not redeem in halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא learns the rules from ״והשיגה ידו״, ״ומצא״ and ״כדי גאולתו״ in ויקרא 25:26.

steps.title: Another ברייתא reads "finds" as something that was there from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading of ״ומצא״ as "new" with the ברייתא about an accidental killer, where ״ומצא״ means someone who was already there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does "finds" really mean something found now? A different ברייתא says the opposite. "And finds" (about an accidental killer) leaves out a person who puts himself in the way. From here רבי אליעזר said: if the stone had already left the thrower's hand, and the other person then stuck out his head and was hit, the thrower is exempt. So "finds" means something that was there from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the same word ״ומצא״ is read the opposite way in a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, ״ומצא״ meant newly found, not already owned. In the killer case, ״ומצא״ means the blade "found" a person who was already standing there. Someone who stepped in only after the stone was thrown is not included. The two readings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: and contrast them; the גמרא sets one source against another
one who puts himself in the way
exempt; here, from going into exile
from the start; from the beginning
evidently; so we see

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. The first ״ומצא״ is about redeeming a field (ויקרא). The second is about an accidental killer (דברים). The question is only that the same word seems to mean opposite things.

phrases.english: Is this to say that "finds" means [something found] now?
But contrast it [with this]:
"And finds": excluding one who puts himself [in the way],

steps.title: Each "finds" is read according to the words around it
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ״ומצא״ takes its meaning from its own פסוק: next to ״השיגה ידו״ it means "now", and next to ״יער״ it means "there from the start".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: in each place we read the word from the rest of its פסוק. With the field, it is like "his hand attains". Just as that is money he gets now, "finds" also means now. With the killer, it is like "forest". Just as a forest is something there from the start, "finds" also means something there from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the clash. The word ״מצא״ has no single fixed meaning. Its neighbor words in each פסוק decide its meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא, ״ומצא״ sits next to ״והשיגה ידו״, which speaks of money he gets now. So ״ומצא״ also means newly found. In דברים, it sits in a פסוק about a ״יער״, a forest that was there all along. So ״ומצא״ means a person already standing there. Both ברייתות stand.

keyTerms.meaning: from the context of the פסוק
similar to; read like
forest

steps.whatToRemember: The same word can mean different things in different פסוקים. We read it from the words around it. That is why ״ומצא״ means "newly found" for the field and "already there" for the killer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא works: a word's meaning is learned from its own פסוק, so two ברייתות can read the same word differently without a real argument.

so too "finds" also means now.

steps.terutzMaskana: Next to ״השיגה ידו״, ״מצא״ means newly found. Next to ״יער״, it means already there. Both readings are correct.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the הקדש leniency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about הקדש and asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "But with הקדש, etc." From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, which allows easier redemption of a field from הקדש. It asks for the source, setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a sold field, the owner may not borrow money to redeem it and may not redeem it in parts. With הקדש, both are allowed. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Property given to the בית המקדש treasury

steps.title: The double word ״גאל יגאל״ allows borrowing and partial redemption
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״ואם גאל יגאל״ that one may borrow to redeem a consecrated field and may redeem it in parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "And if he will indeed redeem it." This teaches that he may borrow and redeem, and he may redeem in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The repeated word ״גאל יגאל״ in the פסוק about a consecrated field shows that redemption is allowed in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have said the word for "redeem" only once. The doubled wording teaches that any kind of redemption works for הקדש. That includes using borrowed money and paying for part of the field at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: "He will surely redeem." The doubled verb in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This leniency is only for redeeming from הקדש. For a field sold to another person, the earlier ברייתא in step 24 still forbids both borrowing and redeeming in parts.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a seller gets his field back for free, so redeeming it is harder
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains the reason behind the rule. Because a sold field returns to its owner at the יובל anyway, the תורה limited how the owner may redeem it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Because we find that one who sells his ancestral field was given extra strength: if the יובל comes and the field was not redeemed, it goes back to the owner at the יובל. So his strength was weakened in that he cannot borrow and redeem, and cannot redeem in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון begins to explain the logic behind the difference. Here he covers the seller's side: he has an advantage at the יובל, so he loses out in how he may redeem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is a balance. The seller already has one big benefit, since the field comes back to him for free at the יובל. Because of that, the תורה does not also give him easy ways to redeem it.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancestral field, inherited family land
The fiftieth year, when sold fields go back to their original owners
His power was made stronger. He got an advantage
His power was made weaker. He got a disadvantage

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Because we find with one who sells an ancestral field
that his power was enhanced,
since if the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed,
it returns to the owners in the Jubilee —
so his power was diminished, in that he does not borrow and redeem,
and he does not redeem in halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reason based on logic to the source from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because a sold field returns for free at the יובל, the seller may not borrow to redeem it or redeem it in parts.

steps.title: A consecrated field is lost to the כהנים at the יובל, so redeeming it is easier
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון finishes his reason. A consecrated field that is not redeemed goes to the כהנים at the יובל, so the Torah made redeeming it easier.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one who consecrates an ancestral field: since his power was weakened, because if the יובל comes and the field was not redeemed it goes out to the כהנים, his power was strengthened, so he may borrow and redeem, and may redeem in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes the comparison by showing the opposite case. The person who consecrates his field loses it at the יובל, so he is given easier ways to redeem it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of the seller. The seller wins at the יובל and loses in how he may redeem. The one who consecrates loses at the יובל and wins in how he may redeem. This explains why the ברייתא's leniencies apply only to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives his property to הקדש
It goes out to the כהנים. The field passes to them at the יובל
Since, because

steps.whatToRemember: Think of it as a balance. Seller: gets the field back at the יובל, so no borrowing and no redeeming in parts. One who consecrates: loses the field to the כהנים at the יובל, so he may borrow and may redeem in parts.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a clear logical reason for why the משנה is stricter with a field redeemed from a person than with a field redeemed from הקדש.
